checkout.label: Payments
checkout.name: Build a checkout
checkout.summary: Take USDC, a digital dollar, from anyone with a wallet. The money is in your wallet in under a second (cashing out to a bank takes an off-ramp), the fee is a fraction of a cent, and there are no chargebacks.
steps: Pay for something the way your customers will, before writing any code.
Read the payment code your checkout sends, then optionally try a payment button in a browser playground.
Ship the order only after your server has checked the payment on the network itself.
Switch to mainnet, decide who pays network fees, and handle the edge cases real customers hit.

after.title: Charge a few cents per API call

paywall-api.label: Pay-per-call
paywall-api.name: Paywall an endpoint
paywall-api.summary: Price each request at a cent or less. Clients, whether people's apps or AI agents, pay inline over HTTP, with no signup, API key or invoice.
steps: Watch the HTTP 402 flow happen: request, price, payment, data.
Read the server that answers 402 with a price and settles the payment, and replay its recorded run on this page.
Pay for your endpoint from a client, run both against a local network, and move the handler into your own app.
Mainnet values, the x402 SDK and a facilitator, and protection for unpaid routes.

after.title: More about pay-per-call
after.summary: How x402 works, facilitators and agents that pay.

demo.title: Paid forecast API · 0.01 USDC per request
demo.success: Paid 0.01 USDC and got the forecast. No signup, no API key.

steps.label: Call the API without paying
steps.description: The server answers *402 Payment Required* with the price (10000 base units, 0.01 USDC) and the address to pay.

steps.label: Pay and call again
steps.description: The client pays 0.01 USDC and retries with the signed payment in the `X-PAYMENT` header, and gets the forecast. Replaying the same payment gets 402 again, and a price above the client's `maxAmount` is refused without paying.

issue-asset.label: Tokenized asset
issue-asset.name: Issue an asset
issue-asset.summary: Create a token for a fund share, a security or a real-world asset, with metadata, an approval list and a pause switch that the network enforces on every transfer.
steps: Approve an investor, send LSF to them and to an unapproved account, and watch the network enforce the rule.
Read the code that creates a Token-2022 mint with metadata, a pause switch and default-frozen accounts, and replay its recorded run.
Create the same asset from your terminal, then approve a holder so they can receive it.
Protect the authority keys, connect your KYC process, and decide who can pause.

demo.title: Lisbon Solar Fund (LSF) · restricted asset
demo.success: 100 LSF settled in the approved investor's account. The 1 LSF transfer to the unapproved account was rejected by the network.

steps.label: Approve two investors
steps.description: Every new LSF token account opens frozen. The issuer approves (thaws) two investor accounts: the first now holds 1000 LSF, the second 0 LSF.

steps.label: Send LSF to approved and unapproved holders
steps.description: 100 LSF to the approved investor confirms. 1 LSF to an unapproved account, still frozen, fails onchain with `Custom: 17` (*Account is frozen*). The run then pauses the asset, which blocks every transfer (`Custom: 67`), resumes it, and uses the permanent delegate to move 50 LSF.
